newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Van den Broek expresses EU concern over Slovakia.
newsitem.headline: Van den Broek expresses EU concern over Slovakia.

text.p: External Relations Commissioner Hans van den Broek raised concerns on Thursday over the democratic process in Slovakia, but said the EU was not considering ending Bratislava's association agreement.

EU officials have already said they were worried by events surrounding the weekend referendum on NATO membership and direct presidential elections that were declared void because ballot papers were invalid.

But Van den Broek, on a one-day official visit ahead of a final assessment next month of Slovakia's eligibility to join the European Union, said any danger of the EU cancelling Slovakia's association agreement was "simply not on.
"It is quite clear that we have noted with concern the events of the past week," Van den Broek said after meeting Deputy Foreign Minister Jozef Sestak.
"We want to clarify and discuss very openly but we want to make clear we are not biased," he said, adding the community wanted Slovakia to be part of the European family.

The twinned referendums were billed as a last chance for Slovakia, which has come under fire from the West for its lack of democratic reforms, to win an invitation to join NATO in the first wave of new members.

Instead, voting degenerated into chaos because of a feud between Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar and President Michal Kovac, who wanted a question about presidential elections on the ballot and prompted a boycott when it was struck off at the last moment.
The Central Referendum Committee declared the widely boycotted weekend referendum void and denounced ballot papers distributed by the Interior Ministry as a "massive swindle".
Van den Broek said that his mission was to clarify points of economic and political questions which are needed for fullfilment of criteria for EU membership.
"This is an important part in time on our discussions as the commission is preparing a report on the preparedness of candidate members," Van den Broek said.
Sestak said discussions with Van den Broek had been "very open, sincere and honest" and added Slovakia was doing all it could to continue moving towards fullfilment of all criteria for EU membership.
